still-untitled/2018-07-30.title: Let Go
stanzas: Let go, loosen the grip,
and watch where the flying sand goes.
The aim is not to grow up by swallowing hurt to keep the peace,
but to find the freedom of release.
Waiting for what,
lingering for what?
Wedged into the axis of time,
it should not submit so meekly.
Release, release,
forget, forget.
These nameless wounds, one after another,
are forever the hero's medals.
Let it be so,
why let longing drive you mad?
There is still time to wander as one pleases,
having waved off the absurdity of youth.

still-untitled/2018-07-31.title: The Rabbit Hole
stanzas: Inside my heart,
there is a place,
called the rabbit hole.
Do you hear the echo?
I am still here,
having forgotten why I began.
I do not want to have nowhere to hide,
I am not afraid of being overlooked,
I only crave a pause from being brave.
The rabbit hole has ten openings,
nine of them are blocked up,
the one that remains cannot be seen clearly.
Still lost on this road,
filled with the jeering of fantasy,
serving my sentence, brains dashed upon the ground.
Silently counting the second after next,
is this spinning a cocoon to bind myself,
or will it be breaking the cocoon, reborn?
A dark cloud drifts lightly past,
it is not announcing that rain is coming,
it has only set its heart on the calm before nightfall.
I was always one who comes and goes alone,
walking between the two ends of a rope,
straining to keep the balance.
The original dream is too lowly,
so simply shatter this mirror image,
the price is going mad for my own sake.
Only a fool is willing to be a good person,
only an idiot gives thanks for being granted a favor,
fool and idiot—which of them is the more sincere!
Some
nameless surge
manipulates fear and strangles all that thrives.
I do not understand,
the lies flying all over the sky,
cloning days gone by, only to come to nothing.
There is nothing to blush about,
if it is for a naked soul,
better to think how to lose control to the full.
Loneliness is the antidote,
dodging is the daily routine,
self-defense is the cage.
Repeated doubt,
excessive trust,
turning the tables, toying with me.
Even knowing how it wounds,
even knowing it is at the end,
even knowing it is already empty.
Still I must strain to say nothing of the pain,
still I must smile and say it is all right,
still I must pretend composure.
Unadorned feeling—
who would care, who would hold it dear,
those faces have scattered away.
What is cut off from the world is hope,
what cannot be touched is warmth,
what shatters at a single blow is impulse.
The sun refracts into seven colors,
not one of them reaches the hole inside the hole,
unless the earth sinks and melts away.
Later the elk run across the snowfield,
palm lines carry on into sea and rime,
spring summer autumn winter, all cut from one pattern.
Nothing matters more at this moment,
all of it is only a lesson in refining,
in order to spare the pointless sacrifices.
The last piece of the puzzle,
savoring clarity,
has waited, and the answer came.
Walking out of fortress after fortress,
setting out the light of the ruins,
releasing all that I had clung to.
Turned into nothing at all,
then grown skilled at making treasure out of waste,
look—the future already.

still-untitled/2021-11-23.title: Expectation
stanzas: With the air that rises and lifts
the sea-waves rise, and close
slipping away under the sun
Dust, whirling in flight
floating with expectation
roaming through a hundred million galaxies
Those born as human beings
follow the tracks of the stars
looking for an end that has no final act

still-untitled/2022-06-19.title: They Say the Wind Blew Last Night
stanzas: It was a day with nothing to do
a cool wind crossed the border and provoked the heatwave
a duel between the young stubborn one and the old stubborn one
each disdaining the other, snatching back and forth
strangers one round, old friends the next, on and on and on
They say, at that moment last night
the fire-clouds stumbled in, still in time
no square, no circle, no sense of propriety
softening, melting into the tender land of the clouds
dazzling and proud, unbridled and dissolute
giving light, giving brightness, giving heat
burn then, every radiance of this world
The fool, equipped with keyboard and mouse
entrusted a whole lifetime of the soul
plugged into the network
passing freely through ten thousand dimensions
creating beautiful dreams alongside reality's rising fervor
Perhaps
one tires of this and that, the square and the round
and seeks a new love, new words, new scenes, new meanings
hands them all to a gust of wind
and another gust
gust after gust
only—there is no need to erase the past
Who the hell knows if there will be wind tomorrow
a breeze or a hurricane
just step aside a little

still-untitled/2022-10-16.title: A Handful of Life
stanzas: Still, silent
I want to bury my head in the lake
to feel the chill of autumn
Fleeting light and passing shadow slip from my fingertips
brushing lightly over the fallen leaves
disturbing the dust
The city, black and white
distorted backdrops and seas of people
the ceaseless flow through cold and heat
So then, add the color back
pick up the graffiti pen
and see what surprises are left
Real, sincere
the worldly wisdom behind foolish words
taken up and put down, a few rounds
A salute to what you believe
to loving what you seek
to the eternal that is the instant
—most beautiful

still-untitled/2022-12-16.title: New Catkins
stanzas: So… rain patters as it falls
So… I can hear my own heartbeat
That was many a midnight's return from dreams
sowing long ago the flight contested and judged in that hour
the passage overgrown with rose thorns
rosemary wrapping and hiding the heaven-sent omen
and so…
All right…
and yet…
the television is wailing
the past is screaming
the hand of god held out a blessing
the mortals received the scorn
everything is still rushing to spread the word
After many years, drawn from the scabbard
the overlapping reflections wear away
beyond space, death and life give their reward
the water of the netherworld sways
joining—

still-untitled/2022-12-28.title: No Man's Sky
stanzas: Sink then  you know this span of time was hard to come by
Toss up a handful of dust  it floats in the air and passes
No one could ever seize hold of those invented memories
Forget then  this was nothing but an accident
not the reunion you wanted  and no surprise either
Fallen asleep  threading the dim street corners and alleys
Sooner or later  we all have to grow used to letting go
No one can be certain of the riddle of time layered with phantoms
No need to meet again  since there are no exceptions
The water clatters and slaps ten feet beyond the window
Envelopes travel between the two extreme poles of the earth
The galaxy turns over  the hands move toward the unknown
The gale has just passed  the soil turns up secrets anew
Those melting breaths
those condensed instants
those silent names
Unchanged  all those traces, deep and faint
Still unfamiliar  those feelings flickering on and off
Reading through the complexity and purity of humankind
imitating the world's contradictions and uniformity
Searching  searching for the meaning at the source
Tracking  tracking the truth of the universe
The utter simplicity of the great Way I crave is more than that
So  I allowed myself to go through it
synthesizing an experience of being there that never stops

still-untitled/2023-01-07.title: The Sequence of January
stanzas: A breeze brushes past the ends of my hair,
the January sun,
is warm.
Travelers passing in twos and threes,
the January leaves,
are still green.
The temperature after Minor Cold,
is just right.
The pulse after losing control,
is steady.
The dancing tongues of flame,
bring no scorching heat either,
the boiling blood,
has slowly run dry.
The blurred smoke,
is feeling the feeling.
A chapter closes.
The first thing is touch,
the second thing is farewell,
the third thing is silence.
The secret lies under the river,
burning, breathing,
and scrambling again…the sequence…
and trapping again…the thirst…
and playing out again…the rupture…
I am the mother of light,
and also the child of darkness,
I am the overlooking of the line between life and death,
and also the color difference between the parallel lines of love and hate,
I am the fragment of a planet breaking apart,
and also the burden of the mayfly in the dust of the universe.
I am delirious joy,
and also weightless oppression,
and the storm that follows from it,
will wipe away everything, everything, everything.
Lie down,
play the music at the loudest volume;
shut myself away,
remember the happiness of long-ago things.
The weather is gradually improving,
the car window is clear and bright as ever.
And so, recovery,
as usual, in good order.

still-untitled/2023-01-13.title: The Place of Meeting
stanzas: The seabed
I am on the seabed
Breathing
I am breathing
there are fish stirring up a hidden mystery
there is the fresh smell of salt
there is sky and earth
Ease
craving ease
Unveiling
imagining the unveiling
there is a veil setting down its pretense
there is rest washing over my face
there is sorrow and joy
Stillness
all of it stillness
Waiting
keeping on waiting
there is a forest burying the small fragments
there is word of what is foreseen
there is black and white
Life and death
beyond the boundary
…exist…
one side withdraws from the world
one side enters the world
The pendulum
does not stop, does not cease
—inside the window
outside the window—
there is only now

still-untitled/2023-01-18.title: Surveying
stanzas: Civilization
it came and went
Epic
it too had its counterpart
Sweeping across
polar night and polar day
Arriving
at the linked axis beyond the stars
Life
pushing up like bamboo shoots after rain
Stroking
the creases on the skin
Enlightenment
pieced together in treacherous wind and cloud
Advancing
the tick-tick-ticking flow of time
At the beginning of Genesis
after the crossing of epochs
listening—
Faith
someone is always keeping watch

still-untitled/2023-08-14.title: Far
stanzas: Far mountains
far waters
far vistas
Far smoke
far thoughts
far journeys
Long and far
far and long
all year long
say it here
everlasting life

still-untitled/2023-08-15.title: Illusion
stanzas: Phantom sound
phantom sight
hallucination
Guess what I
heard
saw
touched
The sea of people is flowing
the white clouds are wandering
the past is void
You are to perceive
and also to overlook
so there is gaining
so there is letting go
so there is letting go and gaining again

still-untitled/2023-08-24.title: Floating Light
stanzas: In floating light I look at the human world
in floating light I look at the motes of dust
gray dogs and white clouds
through the halo
refracting—
the future has already come
what happened sinks away
The simplest of feelings
swallowed the earnestness laid down in advance
you will understand
and you will forget
never once trapped by it
Let freedom and truth run loose
while alive
insist on living
alive in the wind
alive in the rain
let the blazing sun scorch
let all five senses experience it firsthand
Light
light that cannot be grasped
light of a thousand changes
wonder—
the next turn of the wheel
And so
the end of eternity
the endless within the endless

still-untitled/2023-08-26.title: The Pause Button
stanzas: Washed my hair
it rained
fresh
clean
merging with
a perfume smelling of snow mountains
and everything is cleansed
Gravity goes downward
the raindrops follow along
hanging on the car window
the track of time
standing for
the way the story goes
what fate decrees we keep and let go
Our meeting
scattered memories
never gathered into a single page
acting out the false within the real
and afterward…the burden…
The leaves
have slowly yellowed
the migrant birds
are about to leave
people
gather and scatter again
Pause
stay a while
a while of unease
wipe it away hard
try harder still to remember
the heartbeat tells what is alive
—this

still-untitled/2023-10-07.title: Ode to Death
stanzas: One day
I will die
you will die
Yes
we will all die
Scattering into afterglow
falling into stillness
vanishing at last
The star-rings join head to tail
curves and straight lines interweave
the soul comes running out
Look there
stars turned into grains of dust
wandering in the void
—their track
Countless living things are weeping
wailing as they leave civilization
softly chanting the absurd
—chronicle
In the darkness of the polar night
in the prayer of dawn
in the false peace
we are all in…
searching through the fog of illusion
for a thread of undying life
All love and hate will dissolve
all joy and sorrow will go blank
if you can cross over life and death
then you can find yourself
knowing the end
why fear the beginning
make way—the spirit scattered, the soul flown
May it be with a human-like mind
undiminished through the years
that I return to the world

still-untitled/2023-12-12.title: Beyond Heaven and Earth
stanzas: In the wind
in the rain
in the raging storm
letting fate beat down as it will
not caring about the trembling
trying to ignore
burning the words of prayer
Before everything
had not yet come
when love and hate were born
and not yet lived through
when the world's affairs shifted
and went unnoticed
Admit the weakness inside the stubbornness
accept the fear inside the heartlessness
restore what was there before
the flutter of the heart in its truest state
being, unashamed
destroying, resolute
plain and clear
I heard God
all things sway
the outcome was made temporary
the soul passes into another life
transforming into roses, one after another
One sky, one earth
one breath out, one breath in
restlessness and stillness
one person's story
—from beginning to end

still-untitled/2024-02-17.title: The Endless Whirl
stanzas: I have seen you within the endless
I glimpsed you before eternity
all that is not yet knowable
all that is left unfinished
fated and arranged too early
I have walked through the boundless sea of people
I caught the scent of everyday life
there were some fallen flowers and flowing water
there was some heavy snow whirling down
mingled with all that has no bounds
Weariness
—comes over me
Love
—recedes
The tide
—engulfs
Either start again
or turn away
since there is still hope
why give up
Strain once more
meet once more
The walker's footprints
will tread out a life that never ends
Is there a flower bud opening in your heart?

still-untitled/2024-04-11.title: The Oracle
stanzas: Winds of a thousand, ten thousand years beat against my face
at the horizon the first light of dawn suddenly showed
as if…
an unfinished dream
a person walked to the wilderness of the world
A lifetime is this absurd
a single thought is this long
better then…
to crawl in the longing that drives out
to fall silent in the exaltation of the deep doctrine
The cold glint of the polar night
pierced through my heart
time…drains away…
leaving me alone, one breath still left
punishing me, stubborn and on my own
God's extravagance
is neither hurried nor slow
and likewise swaying, drifting
it does not matter that everything is a supposition
even if everything is only an illusion
The sailboat makes its trial voyage in the fog
the golden crow hangs above the purple sea
God said—
only when the last arrogance is overturned
can a truth be found

still-untitled/2024-04-12.title: Who Is Saying What
stanzas: Time is a flood
tearing hard at living things
I do not want…
in the endless cycle of rebirth
to sink into a surge with no focus
The track of every vein
props up the turning of the planet
by accident and by chance, stumbling and colliding
feeling out the autumn harvest and the spring plowing
I want explosion, not equilibrium
fate is merely mediocrity tacked on
the extraordinary only a madness thrown in
The half-hidden, half-showing “ache”
repeating in the rebirth after redemption
do not speak of eternity
it is all scraps left beneath the lies
A gorgeous composure
immersed in boiling water
the pen has sound
graceful and pressed for time
extending another dawn
Manipulation
…so history names it
Launch
resistance!

still-untitled/2024-05-06.title: I Don't Want to Hear Anyone Saying
stanzas: You say
he says
she says
they are all saying
saying I hold on to too much
and I choose to listen to God
because this way
I do not have to listen to what is said
I can
go and live…
the ordinary life of an ordinary person
Every mortal has their own cause and effect
and even God can do nothing about it
the only way is
to cast off the frailty of all living beings
and break open the vastness of intelligence

still-untitled/2025-03-14.title: As Before
stanzas: Some dream much
some sleep little
some are hurrying on
some hesitate and do not move
The streetlamp hides among the leaves
and my thoughts too are half-covered
the bamboo cage hung high
sways with fingertips brushing the ends of my hair
Sometimes the moon wanes
sometimes the moon is full
sometimes relentless wind and rain
sometimes bright sun and blue sky
If the counting goes back and forth within it
and my voice too grows distant
the dark room passed through, stooping low
seeking the truth of the one tender touch

still-untitled/2025-03-28.title: Like
stanzas: Like a morning fog,
with no burning, yet arriving lightly;
no longer entwining, yet near and far at once.
Like an early spring snow,
with no sound, yet rising quietly;
no longer covering, yet melting into the heart.
It never truly parted from you,
and never truly came close to you.
Only lightly, only slowly,
freezing feeling, burying the past.
In an unintended sigh,
in the tears at the corners of the eyes on waking
inch by inch, slowly piling up;
like every word and line in a chat window,
recorded and stacked, still there to be found.
It no longer makes a show, no longer speaks,
taking shape in moonlight, hiding in sunlight.
Not company, yet it stays where it was;
not forgetting, yet unable to hold it in memory.
Like…a beginning,
like…an ending.
Like—this is where it ends,
like—from here it begins.

still-untitled/2026-01-31.title: So
stanzas: Withered stillness — living force
Fearlessness — hypocrisy
To be alive is to follow the heart
To care is to leave yourself no room
On paper the troops are arrayed into a game
In dreams right and wrong are ruled upon
People understood long ago
that the strife will never end
Lies will become truth in the end
and the joke will sink into a funeral
So the meaning of the chase
So…
So, unwilling to settle for this
So, choosing to return
So, wanting to see
a different ending, that is all

still-untitled/2026-02-06.title: The Teeming Multitudes
stanzas: The sun sets — toward what?
The sun rises — inheriting what?
Stars wheel in a nameless vault,
the years turn and turn without looking into themselves.
Without our knowing,
ten million years have run half their course,
time handed on layer after layer,
and who is inscribing where it came from?
How many Earth years, replaced over and over,
bought a single instant —
still, without a sound.
I once dwelt above and watched.
Mountains and rivers rose and fell, finished in one breath,
civilizations flourished and were ruined, like dust and sand churning.
The living run about,
the dead return to zero,
desire and fear cross into a net,
all beings pass back and forth inside it,
each believing they are going forward.
And so the words arise:
Who fixed the starting point?
Who rules on the final stretch?
By what are merit and fame weighed,
and where does a soul get its name?
Having come to the height,
what I saw was ten thousand forms surging.
Flourishing and withering stand side by side,
gain and loss weigh each other out.
No one truly arrives,
and no one strays from the path already set.
Suddenly my line of sight falls,
and I enter the country of flesh and blood.
Cold and heat cling to the body,
day and night are held in common.
In the echo of a heartbeat,
I feel hesitation, pain,
and the one shape that longing wants to leave behind.
I lift my head toward the void.
The place I came from is not declared,
the place I go is undecided.
This finite life —
must it really prove something?
Then the vantage draws back again.
Names and forms come loose,
individuals dissolve,
language loses its weight word by word in the vacuum.
The universe says nothing,
yet keeps on turning,
nebulae turn over,
dark matter resonates slowly —
To exist is simply to be,
not to answer anything,
and the teeming multitudes are only the universe
in one long instant
toward itself
echoing again and again,
a low vibration.

still-untitled/2026-02-19.title: When I No Longer Love You
stanzas: When I love you
you are one of the few exceptions in this life
When I love you no longer
whatever is said is not worth a cent
While I still love
you are the name chewed over and over late at night
When I love no more
I need not hear anything about you
Isn't everyone like this
going through confirmation and doubt again and again
Isn't everyone like this
outlasting the long wait and then giving it up
Everyone is only ever like this
turning affection into bargaining chips
passing desire off as reason
and blaming the whole shortfall on you at the end
We too once understood without words
even our silences could fall into step
back then we actually believed —
that understanding was a refuge
that likeness could hold off every difference
Only later did I see
that what we called our unspoken accord
was only, in each other,
looking for ourselves
Until the filter shattered across the floor
and you saw my selfishness and my evasion
and I saw your calculation and your hesitation
From the joy of first sight to mutual disgust
takes no longer than waking from a dream
Yesterday still held as the only one
today no longer needed
just the distance of turning around
We are only mortals, that is all
In love we enshrine the other as a god
out of love we sentence them to exile in the wasteland
migrating back and forth between extremes
and rarely admitting —
that what really changed
was not necessarily the other person
but that small place inside oneself,
the wavering expectation, the self-interest
How am I to blame you
In this game of binary opposition
you do not even have full autonomy
We are driven by fear
encoded by scarcity
and desire has set our default premises
When I held you as something rare
perhaps I only needed meaning
When I said I give up
perhaps it was only my pride at work
What we call harm
is nothing but two operating systems
in a mistranslation they cannot reconcile
What we call betrayal
is nothing but two value models
in a misalignment that will not run
If one day I speak again of cherishing
may it carry no trace of possession
If one day we each fall to pieces
there is no need to belittle each other
Admit that the brightness and the wreckage
are both a track we walked together
and a lesson brought to completion
Human nature, in this rise and fall,
rehearses over and over,
and between loving and not loving
takes itself apart
It is only, inside a relationship,
little by little,
learning to face things honestly
We are not opposing individuals
only, within the same system,
carriers of different versions
When the fixation recedes
when the roles withdraw
you and I
are nothing but
something in the matrix of cause and effect
briefly lighting up
and then once more
defined

still-untitled/2026-04-11.title: Things Here Are Done
stanzas: Half awake, half oblivious
half in earnest, half greedy for pleasure
I am no one belonging here
I obey no ghost or immortal of this place
I am a guest in the mountains
concerned only with the world's idle ease
Nothing much, and half a life gone by
held to no single form, heaven and earth wide open
Things here are done
like dew, like lightning
no chasing, no hurrying
no debts, no grudges
Not for an outcome, not for name or station
only for a true heart, to have lived it once through
Countless universes, countless versions
countless planets, countless renderings
One is law
one is grace
one is the lesson
one is a worldly bond
Some of me are descending even now
some have already gone far
those on the way need no questioning
those unseen need not be met
This life is only a stretch borrowed
borrowed to look at mountains
borrowed to look at sky
borrowed to see how deep or shallow the human heart runs
borrowed to watch ten thousand forms shift and change
If something was gained, only a few words
if something was lost, only a single thought
Things here are done
mountains and rivers say nothing
this heart faintly bright
fit now for the long sleep

still-untitled/2026-05-30.title: Two Feet
stanzas: People have two feet,
and birds have two feet too.
But people hand their feet to the ground,
and birds hand theirs to the clouds.
From childhood we learn to stand properly,
learn to walk straight,
learn not to fall,
learn to fold a whole life into a road,
and then to run along it with the crowd.
A bird comes down
only in order to rise again;
a bird at rest on a branch
looks as though it were putting the sky
away for a while.
So whether one can fly
does not depend on feet.
Some bodies
were marked by the wind at birth;
some souls
folded their wings too early,
and so mistook the soil for something to lean on.
And so we sew our sense of safety
into the soles of our shoes,
and call the far distance
empty and unreal,
and every lifting of the head
we rename
as impractical youth.
But I still want to know:
if a bird can push off with two feet,
why can't a person
slip lightly free, for one second,
from the weight of an entire life?
Maybe flying
is not leaving the ground,
but that when fate presses me low,
I am still willing —
upward,
toward light,
toward the place that cannot be reached,
to come a little bit higher, a little closer.

still-untitled/2026-05-31.title: Isn't Everyone Born Alone
stanzas: Isn't everyone born alone?
And isn't freedom also a price.
Wind passes through the window gauze,
moonlight falls into the cup,
like a flower that has never spoken.
I used to think
that with someone walking beside me
it would not count as drifting;
later I learned
that some shadows come close
only to keep me company through
one stretch of evening cloud.
Clouds have nowhere to return to,
so all their lives they keep changing;
the sound of the tide never stays,
yet it turns every drawing-back
into an arrival.
And I too was afraid,
afraid the world ran too deep,
afraid that once a heart went down
it would never again recognize
that one grain of star-sand inside it.
But the night comes down layer on layer,
and the stars never speak;
the river goes forward alone
and never asks the silence
for an answer.
Maybe freedom
was never about who lets go of whom,
but the river inside the heart
at last no longer afraid
of flowing toward the boundless.
So you see,
I am walking alone,
and I have not really lost anything.
The starlight is far,
the wind is loud,
and my soul
is opening, out of this human world,
slowly,
into a nameless instant.

still-untitled/2026-06-05.title: Where Am I
stanzas: The same streets
the same flow of people
I no longer want to walk them
nor want to wait
nor care to linger
Those selves that were torn apart,
please piece yourselves together slowly,
don't startle the sound of the wind,
don't wake the daylight either
Let me take my leave
of that damned little longing for too much,
let me fold the long night
into one leaf of a homebound boat,
and give the self that kept sinking
back to whatever comes after dawn
No more asking who owed whom
no more finding a pretext for regret
when the wind passes through
I let go of my name
So those places that split open
were never scars,
only exits I grew for the time being
in order to stay alive
If someone asks where I am
I probably will not say
that I have been saved
I am only living quietly,
like wind crossing a hill,
like moonlight spreading over a sandbar,
watching clouds come and go,
listening to the slow long years
I have learned to keep my own company
and learned
to accept it all
Farther off
there is another me
standing outside the road I came by
long since gone wandering

still-untitled/2026-06-08.title: A Place of Clear Stillness
stanzas: I set my old dreams down at the water's edge
asking neither where they came from nor by what cause
A clear wind passes over the far mountains
and blows a little of the cold from my brow
Only after seeing every lamp of the human world
did I know the bright moon lights the thousandfold worlds
I do not ask the blossom for perfection
I do not ask the dust about sorrow or joy
When a thought rises, let it show itself
when a thought falls, let it scatter
The stream's voice runs past banks of green stone
bamboo shadows sway before an ancient Buddha
This body is still within the human world
this heart has already passed ten thousand gates
Floating fame comes and goes like geese overhead
old thoughts enter the empty pool without a sound
I only lower my head and walk slowly
disturbing no grass or tree, startling no spring
Dusk drapes itself over the empty courtyard at evening
a bell crosses far above the white clouds
I ask no date of return, I ask no year
one censer of aloeswood keeps me company late into the night
If the heart seeks nothing, heaven and earth are wide
I look back: clouds gather deep, the moon grows full of its own accord

yinian/2012-10-24.title: Jiang Cheng Zi · Sleep Talk
stanzas: The water pavilion, as before, shatters the sounds of spring; I long for the road home, I lift the oar and hold it crosswise; met across a thousand li — to meet again would be harder still. Lightly I paint your heart: flying catkins, snow; the flower-tidings wait, wind along the thin corridor.

At the fifth watch my steps drift, smoke and moon a blur; mist in layers, roads upon roads; do not chase what is past — young, we sat and played the sheng. I do not regret treading the waves and hearing sleep-words; your kindness was short, and it wasted a whole life.
notes: Glossary—
Flower-tidings (huaxin): the news of flowers opening, also the season of blossoming; by extension, a woman's youth around the age of twenty;
Treading the waves (lingbo): describing a woman's light footsteps, drifting as though she walked over water.

yinian/2014-11-01.title: Shui Diao Ge Tou · The Month's Beginning
stanzas: A thousand days a traveler walking in rain; jade water rinses the green mountains. Purple mist weaves wind and moon; setting things down in writing, I tread the human world. With you, the airs of Qin carry far; on the Shu road heaven's mechanism turns; for a while I tease the Banished Immortal. Down and out, I stiffen my solitary courage; I brush the sword and shake the Three Rivers.

Welcome white snow fills the sheer ravines; I lodge at Langhuan. The great Peng flies ten thousand li, and still leaves arrogance beaten and speechless. In the common world, banked clouds and clear calm; a fledgling swallow over the dark sea is rarely seen; taking command, I point at the crags. Wild and unbound, I study the classics till my head is white; let tales of gods and monsters be passed along as they will.
notes: Glossary—
Langhuan [láng huán]: in Han Chinese legend, the place where the Emperor of Heaven keeps his books;
Banked clouds, tun [tún]: massed cloud-vapor;
Qingyan: clear and bright, calm and unclouded;
Chanyan [chán]: high and dangerous rock; describing steep precipices and towering stone;
Qiongjing: to study the classics with all one's strength;
Hao: white-headed, old age.

yinian/2014-12-08.title: Yi Jian Mei · Seeking Word
stanzas: No word comes; autumn mountains, a slow fan of coolness. The xiao sobs over frozen buds; on the windy path a zither lifts. Cold bamboo and frosted grass pick at the shade of the window; needlework butterflies; the dream is short, the sky is long.

The disc of the moon fixes its makeup, shy of the blazing river; clear bright banana leaves half hold off the flurry. A cut plum branch shades the water and gathers in the spring sun; the game of go set aside on Penghu, the hidden angelica without peer.

yinian/2014-12-27.title: Nan Lou Ling · Wait for the Next Life to Bind It Again
stanzas: Chasing regret, I look and let nothing slip; I wear out my thoughts on the Biluo Stele. Another new season — off early, east and west. In the end, like lime returning to the four seas, ice and fire refine what is pure and white.

To cheat the world, one fears having too much talent; with too much talent, one fears the world's cheating. Turned solitary — crows crying over the Yi River. Six years searching the vast dream of Nanke, and still I cannot see through the stolen new clothes.
notes: Glossary—

The Biluo Stele: in Longxing Temple within the town of Xinjiang County, Shanxi. It writes oracle-bone script, bronze-vessel script and stone-drum script with the brushwork of small seal script; later generations find it hard to read, and it is a treasure in the history of Chinese calligraphy;
The Yi River: the name of a river. When Jing Ke went into Qin to assassinate the King of Qin, Crown Prince Dan of Yan held his farewell feast here.

yinian/2015-01-16.title: Xi Jiang Yue · Sparse Shadows
stanzas: The pagoda tree's hidden fragrance wakes all at once; the bright lamps burn away the whole of youth. Red walls, green tiles, a bewitching wind hums; the water-clock drips, and waking brings a stifled grief.

In the floating world, feigned madness is not feigned; leaning from a height, the bewitching shadow leaves the dust behind. In the misty blur, crimson and purple lay deep feeling to waste; puppets spread the net of fate.
notes: Glossary—
Jū: a net for catching birds and beasts; to net; to capture.

yinian/2015-02-15.title: Shao Nian You · Wind Sweeping the Last Clouds
stanzas: Flowers crowd, swallows dance, the ink-clouds thin; in a settled age I am as idle as clear ripples. Slow fire brews the tea, a tipsy wind dissolves resentment, the dust settles on a lotus cut from its root.

Merry wandering spends its pleasure, learning stays shallow; at the wayside inn I cut down demons. Wild game and plain gruel, a cold fragrance driving off weariness — who knows I lie moored in a foreign country?

yinian/2015-03-07.title: Feng Qi Zhuo Li · The Waterside Pavilion Hides Its Edge
stanzas: The clear soul wanders loose; the stream's shade is like bleached silk; the summer heat dies in misty weeds. The old man of the mountain strains his wine; the new green brew sets the body's workings in order. He would press an open stratagem half into place, tapping a go stone — great skill in an idle game. Sick of the soft music, the hidden edge dances wildly, and the men of ink give chase.

A blunt arrow pierces the road's dead end; following the clean places, he means to seize the year's business, brief as a drifting cloud. In the water village, a baited hook; across the Five Sacred Mountains, room for a fine steed to run. He demands the altars of the eight wastes, parts the rivers and seas — great order, great plenty. A wrath of a thousand jun grinds down the parasite clerks and thunders out its grand design.
notes: Glossary—
Yanwu: thickets of grass within the mist;
Lujiu: to filter newly brewed wine and remove its impurities;
Lüyi ('green ants'): freshly made wine;
Jishu: a figure for the crucial part of a thing; here it stands for the body;
Suishi: the things one ought to do within a year;
Yunfu ('floating cloud'): brief and quick to vanish;
Duyi [dù]: petty officials who prey upon the people.

yinian/2015-03-10.title: Man Jiang Hong · Why Not Return
stanzas: Horns open new frontiers; the banners are fierce, sand flung ten thousand li. The grey world turns — jackals and wolves hold the road — one man, one horse. In furious battle he holds off the massed soldiers by raw strength; life and death taste full and free, and the nation's shame weighs light. Waiting at the Hu pass, rusted armor offers up a cinnabar heart, and the Qiang flute attends him.

Tear-filled eyes burn, bowstrings press, gravel strikes, straw sandals pinch. The beacon fires send word to the autumn beauty; her longing wastes away. They burn the wreckage and stake everything on wine and meat; the thick night screens off the wavering in them. Taking hold of the old road, counting on fingers until the swallows come home, begging for strings and flutes.
notes: Glossary—
Aozhan [áo zhàn]: fierce, prolonged fighting with an enemy;
Yumu ('fish eyes'): eyes full of tears;
Mangxie: straw sandals woven from the leaves or stalks of plants;
Qiuniang: generally, a clever and gifted woman.

yinian/2015-03-14.title: Xi Chang Xin · Sick with Longing
stanzas: The golden duck censer seethes, the pillow is red silk gauze; the eyebrow brush is bewitching. Xun and chi make scant music and cheapen the height of it; feeling shifts, and carving marks into the candle is toil.

A feigned smile, a light reproach at his intent, lays a good night to waste. Empty cup, fallen leaves, a long-legged spider twirled between the fingers; jade dust and silence alike are hard to escape.
Notes—
Jinya: a duck-shaped incense burner, cast in metal;
Hongxiao: thin red silk;
Xun and chi [chí]: xun and chi are both ancient instruments; played together, their sounds answer each other;
Kela: it is said the ancients carved graduations on candles to measure time;
Yang [yáng]: to pretend;
Chen [chēn]: to be angry, to complain;

Xiaoshao [xiāo shāo]: a kind of spider. A slender-bodied, dark brown spider with very long legs, which usually spins its web between the walls of a room; the web was thought to resemble the eight trigrams and to be an omen of good news;
Suiqiong: jade dust.

yinian/2015-06-21.title: Wang Yuan Xing · Flying on Half a Wing
stanzas: A blizzard on the Tianshan; a thin cold covers everything — with half a wing, east and west are hard to make out. The road runs on and on; we tread on shadows and lose the trail, watching from the side as horses scream and riders are thrown. Soft words worn against each other; the wind tightens, a hidden fragrance breeds warmth; we look at each other and thunder shakes the emptiness. I will keep him company and take my leave of all this splendor.

No way out — the game lost, I yield the blue-green hills; wholly down and out, the brocade furs are loosened. Mist enough, a broken stele; cold light runs riot; the Nine Springs surge and rise in madness. A life of trudging, layer upon layer; the white blank of the wilderness — luckily a fool stays beside me. The vow is left for a thousand ages, the last echo out of the Xiao and Han passes.
notes: Glossary—
Gòu: in ancient usage, the same as gòu, 'enough';
Xiao–Han [xiáo]: a strategic and perilous mountain pass.

yinian/2015-07-11.title: Liu Shao Qing · Innocence
stanzas: The flute falls across a thousand mountains, the dream returns to its native soil, beyond the sky the light is thinning out. Idly I pull at the scenery, willow withes and green vines, winding sorrow and joy together.

The poet's soul chases the drifting mist until it sinks, keeping watch as the flying jade departs, all of it. Turn after turn of the wheel, the blade's edge the same as ever, and yet it has become ordinary.
notes: Glossary—
Diǎo: to draw, to pull.

yinian/2015-07-13.title: Ai Nai Qu · The Hour of the Rooster
stanzas: Resting idly at the bow, I pick up a leaf and listen; the boat girl's song sweeps along the path through the empty wood. Clear ripples change the tune to the pleasure of fishing; a hundred birds chase one another at the sound of the struck fou.
Notes—
Ai nai [ǎi]: the sound of a sculling oar; the sound of singing while rowing; by extension, a song carrying long and lilting;
Raoji [ráo]: a girl of a boatman's family;

Fou [fǒu]: fou is also written with the variant character. According to the Shuowen Jiezi: 'The fou is an earthenware vessel, used to hold wine; the people of Qin drummed upon it to keep time with their songs.' The fou was an ancient Han Chinese clay instrument, and the striking of the fou is mentioned many times in China's ancient texts.

yinian/2015-07-17.title: Hua Fei Hua · Assertion · Words Withheld
stanzas: Assertion
Cloud within cloud, mirror within mirror. Old hatred fades, new joy wakes. Fading like running water that carries the buried blossoms along; waking like spring mud that ought to be offered up.
Again: Words Withheld

He is not he, I am not I. What is left is the track of tears, what remains is the heart's confusion. The track like winter rain resenting the dunes; the confusion like a mountain peach that must keep silent.

yinian/2015-09-04.title: Dao Lian Zi · Waiting
stanzas: The bedding refuses me; I light the sky lamp. Grass and trees rustle — do not listen so closely. We drink the jade nectar together and go looking for the dream-country; against the high wall I fear only leaning there alone.
notes: Glossary—
Qiongjiang: fine wine;
Dian tiandeng ('lighting the sky lamp'): an old Han Chinese festival custom of hanging a lamp from a long pole and keeping it burning from dusk until dawn; it is called a 'sky lamp';
Lingping [pīng]: solitary, alone.

yinian/2015-09-18.title: Ji Xiangsi: Spirit Marriage
stanzas: The shaman shakes the bronze bells; the cool night sways the gold lamp. Knowing the road home, the wind lifts the bridal veil, the colored ribbons light as air.

Waiting for the flying soul to come robed in stars and moon, time falls silent, gathering and stitching the red maples. Longing at its utmost blurs the eyes; though our roads are separate I would go with you, borrowing a way through the netherworld.
notes: Glosses—

Gold lamp: a lamp made of metal. The Han-attributed Record of Fathoming the Dark by Guo Xian: "There is a bright-stemmed grass that at night is like a gold lamp; break off a branch for a torch and it shows you the shapes of ghosts."

yinian/2015-10-03.title: Ku Xiangsi: A Lover's Tears
stanzas: Moon cold on the wutong trees, blade set against blade. At the arched bridge, the frost falls chill. Gathering up the killing air, deep within, the heart burns away the traces of sin. When the hate rises—unreason lies hidden. When the hate is done—no reason in what is left.

Sun warm on the blue smoke, love alone its bondsman. Loose hair breaks free, waist braced against waist. Teasing out a private thought—one promise in this floating life, a game. When the road holds you fast, how do you abandon it? When love holds you fast, how do you abandon it?

yinian/2015-12-16.title: Chang Xiangsi: A Love Bond Across Lifetimes
stanzas: Red robe rushing on, green robe rushing on. Rushing toward the lost ford, ten thousand li of winding road; the camel bells cannot bear to fail it.
By night crawling on, by day crawling on. Far off they tread the frontier, the wind weeping without sound; love and hate lie buried in a foul ruin.
Another
Yellow sand running on, footprints running on. Running on toward longing, to become immortals above; the two of us borrow the wild geese to return.
Moon curving, curving, sky blue and blue. Two cut locks of black hair twine the karma of a former life; meeting is hard, and parting harder still.

yinian/2015-12-18.title: Shuangtian Xiaojue: Winter Solstice
stanzas: The pine stands tall and graceful as jade; time steals the divine brush. Waking, clouds stream past the mountain gate, hurrying the dawn to break, facing the sheer cliff.

The last snow lies in the cool air; the things of the world are schooled to a quiet beauty. Still I remember the fledgling eagle going far away, and pity, long and long, this heaven and earth of past and present.
notes: Glosses—
Green light: time, the passing years;
The cool air (sa li): having the look of coolness.

yinian/2015-12-19.title: Luo Mei Feng: Buying Wine, Meeting a Kindred Spirit
stanzas: The winter wind, bleak and rustling, rolls the white plum; cold cicadas clamor east and west. Umbrellas lost in the sleet and snow collide with a fool for letters—we talk of the ancient books.
So should the noble sons of Wuling be, holding fast the four images, a wonder to see. Wine makes a kindred spirit; we throw our learning wide open, and profit by the gains and the losses.
notes: Glosses—
Buying wine (gu jiu): to purchase wine;
Sleet and snow (xian xue): the larger grains of snow and the snowflakes;
Ancient books (fen ji): the classics of antiquity;
Noble sons of Wuling: youths of wealth and rank;
Holding fast: to hold within oneself (ambition, talent, and the like).

yinian/2016-01-22.title: Chao Tianzi: The Top Scholar in Red
stanzas: The fine horse is draped in red satin; outside the palace gates the peach blossoms burst open. The literary style is lush and lovely—freely now, the wish of a whole life.

Two-staff drums and the blown reed pipes shift and turn together; rank and the robes of office come at twenty, the capping age. Received at the jade hall, the girdle-pendants slow, and spring warms the world of men.
notes: Glosses—
The capping age (ruo guan): in old times a Han Chinese man of twenty was said to be at the capping age;

Girdle-pendants (jin bu): an ornament of antiquity. Jade pendants of various shapes were strung on colored cords into a set and tied at the waist, used at first to weight down the hem of the skirt. Worn while walking, they gave out a sound measured in its pace and proper in its weight. If the rhythm fell into disorder it was held to be a breach of manners, and the ancients took this very seriously.

yinian/2016-03-10.title: Yue Jiang Yin: Eight Years
stanzas: The clear river trickles with dreams of mortal dust—a cut silhouette. Coming and going, it mimics the nature of the mind. Disliking its brightness and cleanness, I sleep among the flowers and wake, and chant the springs and autumns.

Roaming Mount Lan, the ice-soul surges, heaven and man at their play. Old affairs laid one over another—so this is what came of it. Eight years of illness, an idle reflection turned upside down, and what is left is a soul scattered.
notes: Glosses—
Trickles: to run down in drops;
Wake (xing): to reflect upon oneself, to come to awareness;
Heaven and man: heaven and man, the signs of the sky and the affairs of people;
Soul scattered: the soul coming apart and dispersing. It describes the extremes of grief, of joy, of terror, and the like.

yinian/2016-03-11.title: Mingyue Zhu Ren Lai: The Banished Immortal
stanzas: The clear radiance thickens, the threads of wind turn darkly cold; the road home dies away—in the Nine Reaches he hides his form. Indifferent on the Mirage Sea, the flute's note flows into the odes and the hymns. The peacock shuts its screen of feathers; silence.

Drifting catkins in the misted air, holding a grudge, dragging at feeling, sunk in pain. Three lifetimes gone by, and the knot in the heart is only this: disconsolate, thin and worn out—this very night the world of men understands. It is better than riding the cloud and having the crown anointed.
notes: Glosses—
Hiding the form (yi jing): to conceal one's shape and shadow; that is, to live in seclusion;
Nine Reaches (jiu gai): the land from the center out to the eight extremities;

Mirage Sea: a place name in ancient Han Chinese myth. Dongfang Shuo of the Han dynasty of China, in his preface to the Record of the Ten Continents: "I once followed my master on his travels, going as far as Zhuling, Fusang, the Mirage Sea, and the Hill of Dark Night, the Mound of Pure Yang, the region below the First Green, and the abyss of the Moon Palace."

yinian/2016-03-11-2.title: Yangguan Yin: A Thousand Armies, Ten Thousand Horses
stanzas: Shooting at the sun, the Hu sands are lost; armored teams of four chase down the enemy tents. Wolf-smoke bolts to the four quarters; strike the gongs and drums, the war banners sway. Killing in formation, the crows on the walls shriek; lift your eyes—the flying arrowheads bury you. The cries of Long Live are flung away; in the flash of blade and shadow of sword the blood is still hot.

Bearing the order to guard the pass and the frontier, the armor is laid down. A short life, plunging and rising; renown is thin, the general's soul is wide. Strong wine boils a lone courage down; in the bitter fighting, going home is forgotten. Climbing the vermilion stair, the voice of the wind chokes as it bows before the imperial roll.
notes: Glosses—
Armored team of four (si jie): a war chariot drawn by four horses in armor;
Chuang: to strike;

Gongs and drums: the gongs and drums are the four metals and the six drums. The four metals are the chun, the zhuo, the nao, and the duo. The six drums are the thunder drum, the spirit drum, the road drum, the fen drum, the gao drum, and the jin drum. The gongs and drums stand for the signals of marching and of battle;
City crows: the crows on the city wall;
War banner (rong hui): the flag of the army;
Flying arrowhead (fei di): an arrow in swift flight.

yinian/2016-03-12.title: Ye You Gong: Seeking the Path
stanzas: Making karma, the fruit of the immortal tree trembles; dropped into chaos, easy pickings for the demons. Violent, stealing a life, the miasma poisons and harms. Run, run, run—the gate of life is seized, the spirit is fed upon.

Thousand-eyed bodhi seed, it cannot save—boundless, without an edge. Holding the spirit-consciousness back, not daring to drown, chase, chase, chase—the power of the vow is lost, and memory turns mean.
notes: Glosses—
Langgan: the fruit of the immortals' tree;
Thousand-eyed bodhi seed: the thousand-eyed bodhi is an incarnation of the Thousand-Handed, Thousand-Eyed Guanyin Bodhisattva.

yinian/2016-03-12-2.title: Ding Fengbo: Made Chancellor (on Yu Qian)
stanzas: Beacon fires linked in a chain break the rule of the age; body ground to powder, bones broken, he sets the foundation of the state. A hundred days of siege and he was not afraid at all—straight at it—rooting out the treacherous and the fawning to hold the capital.

Since antiquity it has been hard to withdraw once merit is won—one intent only: sooner break than bend, measured against a grand design. Loyalty and honor both kept whole, given back to the histories that came after—he died for the state—and in life and after death, gain and loss are a small matter.
notes: Glosses—
Foundation of the state: the root and base of the country;
The great departure: to die for one's country.

yinian/2016-08-06.title: Xiaozhen Xi Fan: Drifting Snow
stanzas: Bandits ride the passes at will; the spirit handed down from the old days reveals a heart true to another. On the city wall, grown old, the winter-enduring flower calls out. Going on to fight the Wolf Star again, the snow cools the steady dark eye. Rousing the ancient road, Liaodong is still a blur of white.

Lift the long sword, smear blood in oath before the Lord of Heaven, one cup shared through the treacherous ground and the smooth. To the end of what life is left, wash the violence and upheaval clean, and haul back the Central Plain by main strength, far into time. On the road of strangers we look once more: at the mound of the heroes, only the warmth of gunsmoke remains.
notes: Glosses—
The wind handed down (liu feng): the customs passed down from earlier generations;
To reveal one's heart (jian dan): to meet another with complete sincerity.

Winter-enduring flower (ren dong): the honeysuckle; because when its old leaves wither and fall at the end of autumn new green has already sprouted in the axils of the leaves, and it does not wilt through the winter, it is also called "ren dong," the winter-enduring;
Wolf Star: also named the Dog Star; by old accounts it stands for invasion and plunder;
The dark eye: the black pupil held at the center of the socket. It signifies steadfastness;
A blur of white (mi man): describes smoke and dust, or wind and snow, filling the whole sky and covering the ground in one vast haze;
Treacherous ground and smooth: the perilous and the level.

yinian/2016-08-07.title: Nan Xiangzi: A Spring Day
stanzas: The spring day holds a deep sweetness; greedy for the frogs' cry that sees off the tender cold. Egrets and grasses pale and adrift, the lake's face lazy, all dappled. Three thousand scrolls of poems draw open a grotto-heaven.

The pale guest keeps company with the tea's smoke, bestowing the favor of daylight, playing in the countryside. In the dream a clear sound folds into a realm transfigured, shed of the common. Letting the heart go free, I invite the five immortals.
notes: Glosses—
Pale guest: another name for the pear blossom;
Bestowing favor (chong jie): to grant honor and reward;
Among the grasses: a figure for the countryside;
Realm transfigured (hua jing): language turned into a realm of its own;
Five immortals: the ghost immortal, the human immortal, the earth immortal, the heaven immortal, and the divine immortal.

yinian/2016-10-19.title: Poluomen Yin: Drifting Clouds
stanzas: A fresh touch of autumn; the cold wind sweeps it all away and leaves it bare. All at once the press of things comes surging. One vein of longing will not be given up; even the long night is glad with it. This going wounds a wish long held; the red sash streams in the driving rain.

Who is there to cancel it out? I sigh: of all things, the waiting is the farthest off. Out beyond the town the reed flowers shiver, and the dusk is bright and plain. Strung and knotted, this bond of feeling; soul laid over soul, and after it all only a lost bewilderment remains. I cherish the road home, and will not talk on and on.
notes: Glosses—
Kong zong: affairs thronging and pressing;
Xiao xiao: describes wind and rain driving hard;
Reed flower (di hua): a perennial herbaceous plant, shaped like the reed;
Strung and knotted: threaded on a cord and tied fast. It describes something held firmly in mind;
Lao lao: the look of one disconsolate, as though at a loss.

yinian/2016-10-28.title: Zhuying Yaohong: The Bride
stanzas: Candle shadows sway red; she draws the dark brows, brushes the apricot cheek, pins up her hair with jade. Bamboo reeds play the years far away; hands joined, she hides the scented tear-stains.

The curtain stirs, the mandarin ducks blaze bright; the phoenix crown hangs low, the crossed cups linger and cling. One night, one lifetime—what joy that the bond is tied, feeling drawn so tight it will not be exchanged.
notes: Glosses—
Apricot cheek: describes a woman's beautiful face, white with red showing through;
Scented tear-stains: tear-tracks carrying the fragrant powder;
Qian quan: 1. firmly tied; not coming apart. 2. deep in affection.

yinian/2016-10-31.title: Yi Han Yue: Return to the True
stanzas: Gazing far at the distant mountains, the lance held crosswise; one by one the great catastrophes come loose. The causes and effects of the dust of before are all of them ordinary; surpassing the desolation, the karma that remains.

In the vast sky a white egret cries; I strike the sword's scabbard, and the spirit is turned over and over. In the dream of this floating life, impermanence is the teaching; seeing through the road of fate, I go free and unstinting.
notes: Glosses—
Lance held crosswise (heng shuo): describes a bold and heroic bearing;
Zhui gen: to surpass;
Free and unstinting (hui huo): unrestrained, easy and unbound.

yinian/2016-11-06.title: Pusa Man: Watching Chan
stanzas: Out of nowhere the jade rain dissolves the stray thoughts; I see straight through the divine tune and follow its manner. Sitting withered, all at once a light-year, and clear understanding is here before the eyes.
Level and upright, I swallow the vastness; the nature of emptiness shows itself as it will. This place here is the Buddha-heaven—what need is there to keep returning without end?
notes: Glosses—
Jade rain: the rain of pear blossoms;
Buddha-heaven: as good as the Western Heaven, that is, the Land of Utmost Bliss spoken of in Buddhism.

yinian/2016-11-14.title: Wang Xian Men: The World's Beginning
stanzas: Ten thousand layers of cloud-wall break the immortals' gate; the final kalpa arrives. The unbroken rope-way twists through the traces of moss, breathing out a dark dusk.

Vast and faint, the pine-surf fierce; a startled swan opens up the lost ford. The sword's light sweeps all before it and turns the wheel back. Turns the wheel back—the wind's sleeve gathers up the broken soul.
notes: Glosses—
Final kalpa: a Buddhist term. It means the kalpa of the last dharma, one kalpa to a thousand years;
Jiong jue: as good as saying unbroken; having the look of never ceasing.

yinian/2016-11-17.title: Tianmen Yao: Asking the Way
stanzas: Seeking the Way in the Realm of the Three Pure Ones, crossing the sky-moat—jade towers of shimmering light. The evening drum intones; from the wide cliff a flying spring comes gushing.

Waiting for the cloud-wrapped peaks to open again, the rose-clouds gathering and shining, to be ferried across—the true scripture, the offering of the three treasures. Famed traces remain; so I ask after the Dharma, wearing myself away in pursuit of light and shadow.
notes: Glosses—
Realm of the Three Pure Ones: the highest place in the heavens;
Shimmering light: a glittering radiance;
Cloud-wrapped peaks (yun xiu): ridges wound about with cloud and mist;

Three treasures: the three treasures first appear in Laozi's Daodejing: "I have three treasures, which I hold and keep. The first is compassion; the second is frugality; the third is not daring to be first in the world. Being compassionate, one can therefore be brave. Being frugal, one can therefore be ample. Not daring to be first in the world, one can therefore become the chief of all vessels."

yinian/2016-11-18.title: Huaqing Yin: A Deep Vow
stanzas: Slender pale hands raise the cloud-zither; no end to the endearments. In the precious censer the heart-character coils; the red plum, breathed in, is thick with meaning.

The soft wind comes in flakes and wearies the flowered courtyard; the jade one, half vexed and half laughing, quick and light. Waiting until the fragrant dew is sipped away, the snow on the branch melts into clear weather.
notes: Glosses—
Heart-character: heart-character incense, incense laid out in the shape of the character for "heart";
Chen xiao: on the point of laughing, on the point of taking offense.

yinian/2016-11-22.title: Qiliang Fan: Weeping in the Snow
stanzas: Bleak and bleak, cutting and cutting; the whirling wind roars, and dark wolves to left and right, seeing clear and full of doubt. Palms open, fingers stiff and straight, tears wet the bloodied armor, lips locked, eyes split wide. The spirit scatters and goes out; a hand's breadth away, a burning love becomes eternal night. The frozen clouds grieve; a thousand birds are gone from the sky; the empty snow is like dust and chaff.

Looking back to where the years went, breathing on cold hands, brows lowered, that one at my side. The ice-wheel shines as it always did; off to another country—what can be done with what is broken? I dream my way to the Lantern Festival: painted boats, lion dances, the heat of the lamp market. I fear that now, through ten thousand years and a thousand autumns, point by point it falls away.
notes: Glosses—
Ming huo: clear discernment and doubt;
Fingers straight: the fingers cold and stiffened;
Frozen clouds: the dark clouds of deep winter;
Dust and chaff: a figure for what is slight and not worth regarding;
Ge nong: that person.

yinian/2016-11-26.title: Wushan Yi Duan Yun: The Sky Clears
stanzas: Lifting the oar to slap the white waves, unhurried the migrant birds move on. A single leaf of a boat draws near Mount Wu. The clear-day haze takes harm from the first cold.

Old affairs, a thousand hammerings and a hundred temperings; creation will not bear being schemed over. Better to let go and enjoy what is here—hoist the sail, and of itself the whole view opens wide.
notes: Glosses—
Zhao: an implement for rowing a boat;
Pian zhou: a small boat;
Clear-day haze: the mist in the mountains on a fine day.

yinian/2017-01-28.title: Si Di Xiang · Knowing Grace
stanzas: Swiftly, swiftly — what remains of Tai Yi wanes. The auspicious crane comes back along the road it came, bearing the bright glow.
Musing on the mortal world and the heavens above, I tell the flowing pearls through nine reflections. A withered tree that has passed through no winter and no summer — how shall it put out a branch?
notes: Glosses—
Tai Yi: what the Daoists call the Dao; in antiquity, the origin and the substance of all things in the universe;
Waning: the passage of a thing from flourishing into decline;
Flowing pearls: the prayer beads of Daoism, which were at the earliest called 'flowing pearls';

Nine reflections: Analects, 'Ji Shi': 'The gentleman has nine reflections: in seeing, he considers clarity; in hearing, acuity; in his expression, warmth; in his bearing, respect; in speech, good faith; in affairs, diligence; in doubt, asking; in anger, the trouble to come; in gain, what is right.' Later used broadly for turning something over and over in the mind.

yinian/2017-01-29.title: Ding Xi Fan · Sealed in Dust
stanzas: In the blink of an eye, years and months pile up; the affairs of the world — whipping up the dust of the campaign, tempering the lines on my brow.
Light cavalry — on whom do they rely to cross the desert? Clashing weapons startle the depths of a dream. Again I see the desert poplars cracking in the wind, sweeping the yellow clouds.
notes: Glosses—
Crossing the desert: to pass over the sands;
Yellow clouds: the clouds of the frontier. In the desert country beyond the passes the yellow sand flies up and the sky is often yellow, hence the name.

yinian/2017-01-30.title: Xi Fen Fei · Facing the Snow
stanzas: Call up the primordial and this love does not age; facing the snow we keep to each other at the sky's corner. Only the red flower is fair — hardened by the weight of frost, it offers all the more to lean on.
In brow and eye lies hidden a treasure rare in this world; may the divine lord be willing to grant his favour. The froth of splendour pales and dwindles; one whole heart frets at nothing but parting.

yinian/2017-02-01.title: Lian Bo Ming · Passing the Tribulation
stanzas: At Naihe Bridge the wind lifts all at once — I know it is Granny Meng sighing. Ill-fated mandarin ducks, we forsake the Hall of Rebirth. On the bank of the River of Forgetting we linger, fireflies point by point, the Buddhist chanting a clamour — a hundred years, vast and far.

The six paths of rebirth — we whip the horses through the dark peril. Wading on through a red rain of petals, through Yama's thronging ranks, the fire-crows wan and dim. Beyond this place, the udumbara's fragrance spreads long.
notes: Glosses—
梵呗 [fàn bài]: in Buddhism, the sound of singing and hymns of praise performed at a rite;
Wading on: to walk along steeped in (muddy water);
Fire-crows: crows of legend that can carry fire in their beaks.

yinian/2017-03-10.title: Bie Yuan · Hushed
stanzas: Peach-coloured lamp blown out, close by the door leaf — the heart's business standing all alone. The crystal curtain is about to come down; a chrysanthemum pin binds her hair, her steps light and full of grace; loose sheets of flowered notepaper send the wine's madness off.

I will not see my lord away; rouge-stained tears blur and spread the grief of parting. At the cold pond the horse is given water, a withered vine holds a dragonfly fast. Bitterly I pity the qin and the se gone mute; the gilt beast turns cold, and day is about to break.
notes: Glosses—
The grief of parting: the thoughts and feelings of separation;
Watering the horse: to give a horse water to drink;
The gilt beast: an incense burner in the shape of a beast.

yinian/2017-04-09.title: Qian Qiu Sui · An Instant
stanzas: A soft coolness stirring — what an idle savour this is. The withered grass revives, casts off the crickets. Golden light streams through the last of the mist; we talk over the histories of romance. The histories of romance — before the languorous tune is finished, the Green Gate lies in ruin.

We ride until the cinnabar cliff stops us, gaze to the limit on the ranked mountains, and are drunk. Shoulder to shoulder, inside the new sun. The geese drop low to take the measure of the stranger; together we watch a thousand thousand years. A thousand thousand years — cloud unfurling, cloud furling, leaving no trace behind.
notes: Glosses—
Revives: to wake again, to recover;
The last of the mist: the mist that remains;
Take the measure: to look over, to judge.

yinian/2017-07-18.title: Sao Di Wu · Nine Nines Return to One
stanzas: Throw the cold water, boil the hot water, cold then hot and the empty lane comes to a boil. Work the raw earth, plant the wild flowers. Sprawling gourd vines drum at the glad rain, fruit-fragrance brimming over.

The sweeping-the-floor dance, the wiping-the-floor dance, sweeping and wiping and good things on the way. Lay in the qin and the inkstone, set out the wine and drink a wish. Nine years of one heart, coming and going — the old friends gather.

yinian/2017-08-20.title: Sha Sai Zi · Converging
stanzas: On all four quarters an empty, sunken cold green; mist blows across the tent, and the Dragon Sands draw near. Have I trudged all these years, with no other?

I lift a cup of libation, clear as snow, slip through the caves and crevices, praise the gorge at its end. Bending wind and thunder to my carriage, I wind through the peril and turn it into the world's far edge.
notes: Glosses—
Dragon Sands: broadly, the sandy desert country beyond the frontier;
Trudging: the hard labour of journeying back and forth;
Wind and thunder: fierce wind and violent thunder.

yinian/2017-08-21.title: Wu Tao Yuan · One from a Former Life Comes Visiting After
stanzas: On the field path they gather the plump lotus root; a child in horn-braids takes the hill ridge in their arms. Washing clothes, the stone and the club are busy; the erhu lifts.
Apricot porridge ladled out fragrant; sweet wine softens the winding gut. By borrowed moonlight they work the shadow puppets; the wild bridge is cool.

Horn-braids: short braids done up on either side of the crown of the head like a pair of horns;
砧杵 [zhēn chǔ]: the laundry stone and the beating club;

yinian/2017-10-16.title: Shui Diao Ge · Tracing the Source
stanzas: The sun and moon of the mortal world go and come back in their flowing; vast and dim, a thousand mountains show no end. Three lifetimes are absurd dream enough — I mean to put it to the assembled immortals and ask them why.

yinian/2017-10-17.title: Qing Shang Yuan · The Man of the Rotted Axe Handle
stanzas: The wind stops, the urgent waves entwine their necks; the passes and rivers press and hurry the farewell on. The road ahead runs south, runs north; deep in the night watch I wake on a lonely pillow.
Still I say: take care, take the greatest care — courting your dislike, this feeling surges up. This going has no date of return; all that needless coaxing, day after weary day.

yinian/2017-10-18.title: Xiao Qin Wang · Breaking the Line
stanzas: A zhang of frost on the blade stirs up the black cloud; feeling the cold, the scented tear-tracks touch the crimson lips. The raging horses hurl themselves all-out and crush the wings of the line; at daybreak, for whom is the bell's talk under the eaves to be heard?

Wings of the line: the two flanks of an ancient battle formation;
At daybreak: when the sky grows light;

yinian/2017-11-07.title: Bai Xue · Forgetting the Dust
stanzas: Snow drives hard on the eaves and the steps, and passes — it is over — the floating life on the pillow, faint and half-remembered. I look level into the hazy wilds, keep watch alone over the disordered years, and — ah! — how many daybreaks. Before ever I have heard it, the north wind rises, falls again, and settles, settles. Only just now, after so long, do I gather up my scattered thoughts; a goose broken from the line is ready to fly west.

Leaves over all the ground, cold and cheerless, wear away the shadow I turn to look at, rubbing the airy void between my fingers. Everywhere in sight the scenes of a mirage tower; laughter and play cover the sound of the strings. With light, swaying steps — you and I as we were then, pointing under the moon at a far peak. A sudden breath blown at the cold ash of the candle, and the frost-white drains the last of that foolish love away.
notes: Glosses—
駃 [kuài] snow: snow that comes down with fierce force;
了 [liǎo]: to conclude, to end;
The hazy wilds: describing the blurred, boundless look of open country;
Gather up: to set in order, to rouse oneself;
The heart's bent: consciousness;
撚 [niǎn]: to rub and knead between the fingers;
寒灺 [hán xiè]: the burnt-out ash of a candle on a cold night.

yinian/2017-11-17.title: Liu Zhou Ge Tou · Heaven Beyond Heaven
stanzas: Years among the mountains; from far off I recall half a life of wildness. Drew the sword and went; the river lamps spread wide. Walked strange countries, knew what it was to sleep on stone, forced the nine bends of stream and marsh. The pine-surf sounded, sand and gravel scalded, the stars burned bright, I waded the linked peaks, the moon like frost. Ape-shadows dogged my tracks, rainbow rain heaved up waves of cloud, catkins and leaves flew every way. Sails hoisted for ten million li; dream-talk out of a childhood bed. Each thing an ocean, scattering off into the vast and dim.

Going or staying without limit, an even heart gives way. I look out past the sky — just now cool and clear. The lone traveller is let loose, the long world forgotten; reckon the cause as it is due, the fruit is hard to carry off. Below my eyes I climb the height, lean beside the immortals' halls, and draw in the jade fragrance. The wind blows for a while; the langgan fruit comes down; beside the purple spring I step through the Final Gate, my heart turning home toward the Great Way. It keeps me company through the eight directions, yet throws off the mortal world's reckonings; I stand still for the first sun, and the cold cicada cries and cries.
notes: Glosses—
River lamps: the lamps on the boats out on the river;
Hoisting sail: to raise the sail;
Without limit: having no restriction, having no end;
Langgan: the fruit of the immortals' tree;
Purple spring: the spring water the immortals drink;
The Final Gate: the three gates of Chan — the first gate is awakening to the Way, the second gate is cultivating the Way, the final gate is realizing the Way;
螀 [jiāng]: the cold cicada.

yinian/2017-11-19.title: Tan Chun Man · Saxaul
stanzas: Half a sheet of paper for a life, one ball of wine-fumes, blended with the cold clear light. Cattle and sheep beyond the frontier, the slanting sun watched into old age — no more than yesterday's gladness. Slack and tired, I lie along the eaves-tooth, bare feet braced, alone in its deep quiet. Let the common world part and run where it will; tomorrow is still the locust-tree dream.

Don't blame the winter plum for failing early, nor the hungry birds for pecking it all away — in the end it is their nature. The long song of ten thousand ages, looked at from now, has never had its true savour turned over and sung. Again I hope for next year's spring, afraid, only afraid, of staking my life for nothing. What of it, then? Then let the four seas be made over!
notes: Glosses—
Saxaul: a sand-fixing plant that grows in sandy ground;
Eaves-tooth: the part of a roof's eaves that juts up like a tooth;
The locust-tree dream: see 'the Huai'an dream'; a figure for life being a dream and wealth and rank being impermanent.

yinian/2017-12-29.title: Shuang Rui Lian · Half Understood
stanzas: Bright gossamer floats over the sleeve-guard; the mind is still and shy of the cold mist, and the idle heart keeps a remnant of waking. The lotus nods its head; twin blossoms on one stem sway their shadows, bashful. But then cool thoughts pull at me, and I cannot bear to look — the dust of the past lies heavy. I raise the sword in farewell; willow-down wheels and dances, the dawn cock takes up the mood.

Long ago I forgot that the years have no edge; far off the waters lie level, watch after watch all the same. Let the wing-to-wing birds be — the lovely days squandered on indulgence. Still I love the warm wind across my face; I gaze away in sorrow — the life to come is unsettled. The green canopies stir, whispering; the evening sounds, the pavilion cold.
notes: Glosses—
Bright gossamer: the drifting threads spun out by insects, floating in the air;
Sleeve-guard: a covering worn over the sleeve;
廻儛 [huí wǔ]: to wheel about in flight and dance;
Watch after watch: one night watch, and then another;
鹣鹣 [jiān jiān]: the birds that fly wing to wing;
The lovely season: the time of beauty;
Green canopies: lotus leaves.

yinian/2018-01-02.title: Qing Bei Ling · Finding Delight
stanzas: A snap of the fingers and the years flow by; with no mind for it I set down a stone, and lying back watch the painted screen run through its illusions. On the long spring day I boil tea and prune the branches; the aloeswood sends up its scent and dizzies the eyes.

The pipa's thin string plucks up a clear song and a sigh; cup in hand I covet the mortal world's remoteness. The cool moon half lights the red rain of petals; ink on the hand makes plain a heart bound fast in tenderness.
notes: Glosses—
The long spring day: a day of spring;
Aloeswood: the sinking incense-wood;
The thin string: the fourth string of the pipa, and by extension the pipa itself;
The cool moon: the moon;
Remoteness: distant, far away;
Red rain: fallen blossoms coming down like rain.

yinian/2018-01-03.title: Cheng Tou Yue · No Way
stanzas: Swiftly the swaying green boughs whip up the dust; all at once I remember a tune beaten on red sandalwood. Wandering alone under the moon, a goldfish leaps in, teasing the rippled light into warmth.

From now on the resolve in these jade bones lives on; in silence there was once a meeting of minds. The silver worm of the lampwick curls on itself, the pine gate has long been shut, and the axe handle, rotted through, props up the mood of parting.
notes: Glosses—
Swaying green: flowering branches in motion;
Red sandalwood: the name of an instrument, clappers made of sandalwood;
迤逗 [yǐ dòu]: to tease, to entice;
Curls on itself: of a thing, to wind around itself;
Silver worm: the snuff-flower of a lamp;
The rotted axe handle: the handle of the axe has decayed — a figure for a great span of time.

yinian/2018-01-14.title: Mo Shan Xi · Unbridled
stanzas: Clear wind, bright moon, washing clean the traveller in the dust. Qin notes wind round the stream and the hills; the lone shadow breaks, and bees and butterflies keep teasing it. Drifting through the blue-green mist, my sleeves loose a divine fragrance; the shower lets up, the rushes and reeds sway, and heaven and earth widen as the heart wills.

A whole life in exile — no matter that talent and name are buried. The common world ought not to intrude; a deep dream is good, let it fall where it falls. Early autumn is cool and easy; I lie high between the water and the cloud, awake as though drunk, and laugh at others: why go on searching so bitterly?
notes: Glosses—
Rushes and reeds: cattail rush and reed.

yinian/2018-01-31.title: Guo Lang Er Jin Pai · Playing Against Myself
stanzas: Into the mood: spread open a wind-shaken splendour, hold the breath and tap down a stone — not easily taken. There is delight in it, waiting to break the rules. All my life a long grievance, east and west, that would have Heaven gather every affair into one.

Overturning: shifting and changing without constancy — from the first, one's own nature is hard to refuse. Borneol rouses the spirit; inside the game, an illusory scene; I lay the plans and set the order out. What was neglected in old days, the far days, come round again; a new waking, quiet and unbroken, follows the welcome rain.
notes: Glosses—
飐 [zhǎn]: to shake and tremble in the wind;
Borneol: also called dragon's-brain incense, or bingpian;
New waking: having just woken from sleep, or a fresh understanding;
Quiet and unbroken: having the look of stillness;
The welcome rain: rain that falls just when the crops most need water.

yinian/2018-03-30.title: Ye He Hua · No Words
stanzas: Slow steps, the song at its end; the dream leaves its old traces behind; a whole body of dusk only just coming on. A heaven and earth inside the pot smooth out the cold light of the sword's shadow. Rain wets the magnolia's scent; the flower-blowing wind beats at the blood-stained coat and cools it. To have seen the scorched earth, to have known what a life is — all of it in one moment of panic.

Three rolls of the rattle-drum fly up, hurrying me back to my senses; a small stone, clear and bright, in the quiet pond. My heart carries an age of chaos; what can such care do but hide itself deep? If an old friend were beside me, I would keep you company through the years and the festivals and never know their length. To take leave of all that ties me, I follow you off into the distance, and guard your peace and health forever.
notes: Glosses—
Ye he hua: also called the night-fragrant magnolia;
迸鼓 [bèng gǔ]: a rattle-drum.

yinian/2018-04-11.title: Bu Suan Zi · Coming Home
stanzas: I drink off the bitterness in the wine and take back the face I wore before. I mean to open the mountain and cut down the evil souls — scarcely enough to feed the podao its fill.

Rhinoceros-hide armour shines in the mermaid-fat candlelight; the last leaves are swept before the wind. My one fear is that I cannot see the thing through to its end; I knock and beg the blue heavens to keep me.
notes: Glosses—
朴刀 [pō dāo]: an old-style weapon, a blade narrow and long with a handle shorter than that of the great sabre, wielded with both hands;

Mermaid candles: candles made from the fat of the mermaid. The phrase comes from the Records of the Grand Historian, 'Basic Annals of the First Emperor of Qin': 'When the First Emperor was buried at Mount Li… they used mermaid fat for the candles, reckoning they would burn long without going out.' Wang Penggui of the Tang, 'Rhapsody on the Sun': 'Fireflies gather and burn, the mermaid candles blaze together; the bright moon shines from on high, the myriad stars are ranged afar.' Dai Wangshu, 'The Lamp': 'The emperor lies long, the mermaid candles burn high and eternal, in his dark and solemn tomb.'

yinian/2018-04-12.title: Feng Ru Song · Music and Song at Midnight
stanzas: Tall bamboo sways its shadows, wind runs through the pines, and it sounds like a sheng being played. Before the moon I brush the sword and taste the quiet of the heart; the past has gone cold — how could one bear to cherish that ache? Year round the banked snow never melts; has the departing wild goose ever once come to rest?

The sound of oars goes far off, and another winter comes; training the horse, I struggle to move on. Remembering: on the meditation couch the tea-mist rises, talk in the wind, laughter, the sincerity of being young. I staked everything of half a life on one throw; grown old, I find instead that I delight in having nothing to contend for.
notes: Glosses—
the sound of oars (ná yīn): the noise of oars in the water;
training the horse (diào mǎ): to tame and train horses.

yinian/2018-04-14.title: Zui Gongzi · A Traveler in the Dust
stanzas: A breath blows out the dream, and the lone lamp dies. Propped on the pillow, the slight drunkenness burns fierce. The loosened hair-knot drops into the flowering thicket; on the clamorous street the carriages and horses press hard.

In the curve of the brow the rancor will not rest; sick with wine, I press down the knot in the heart. Weary eyes, the cup drained to nothing — Zhuang Zhou's butterfly takes its business to the green vine.
notes: Glosses—
lone lamp (qíng): a solitary lamp;
chéng: so drunk that the senses are muddled;
sick with wine: sunk deep in drink;
wèn: to press down; to steep, to submerge.
