yinian/2018-05-23.title: Xiao Chong Shan · Early Summer
stanzas: Unbroken rain ploughs flower-shapes from the mud and splashes the star jasmine; the tiled house brims with apricot and plum, and the willow orioles are urgent. The green conch of the hills drowns the words of the soft red world; seeking the savor of being alive, I fling ink along the threads of wind.

Drowsy waking steals the mornings and the evenings; the thick clouds gather and scatter again, and the sick face takes its leave. Range upon range of mountain color, half of it lost in haze; the kun's string plays on, sweeping away both the right and the wrong.
notes: Glosses—
unbroken rain: rain that falls on and on without stopping;
plough-flowers: earth turned up into the shapes of flowers;
star jasmine: an evergreen woody climbing vine;
green conch: a figure for green hills;
soft red: the red dust, the mortal world;
mornings and evenings: dawn and dusk, from day to day;
thick clouds: heavy, densely layered cloud.

yinian/2018-05-29.title: Zhexian Yuan · Heaven's Decree
stanzas: The green lamp not yet burned to ash, the solitary heart shifts and becomes cool wind that wakes the spirit. Having passed through all the flowering and falling of the world's splendor, the allotted life of the soul tilts aslant, floating and sinking.

Where I stand is not illusion and yet seems illusion; my abiding wish is a thousand times true, ten thousand times true. Night rain dwindles away into sleep and dream; the drifting gossamer, ailing yet forcing itself on, grows dim and dim.
notes: Glosses—
aslant (qī xié): tilted, leaning over;
abiding wish: the aspiration one has always held;
dwindles (lánshān): waning, falling away;
drifting gossamer: a figure for the workings of the mind;
forcing itself on: to act, and keep acting, while carrying an illness.

yinian/2018-06-18.title: Zhezhi Yin · Far Off
stanzas: A march of two hundred, and a wild wind rising; we pitch camp where we stand. The blade goes back in its sheath, and there is no thread of thought to follow; strand by strand the bili pipe says what the heart feels.
notes: Glosses—

zhè (the cudrania of the tune's title): a deciduous shrub or small tree, the bark gray-brown and set with long thorns, the leaves ovate, the flowers in rounded heads, the fruit globular. Its leaves can feed silkworms; the root bark is used in medicine;
bili: a wind instrument played by the nomadic peoples of the north, shaped like a horn, its sound mournful.

yinian/2018-06-26.title: Lu Hua · Mortal Thoughts
stanzas: Splendor is shallow, shallow; a touch of sorrow-forgetting incense tints the air, and the business of dreams grows distant. Here a place of revelry, there a place where red silks vie in beauty. This feeling, this scene, just so; this memory, this moment, dispersing. It was never more than this: a person is a blade of grass, and what one asks for is the plain and the quiet.

Petals wind themselves about the robe; the moon that has no equal is not yet done, and thought falls away and sinks. Who fears half a life as a prisoner; who is here for the sake of a first meeting. If you mean to overturn heaven and earth, you can still give battle with no pieces left on the board. I look for some pleasure: the flying white takes in every cold gaze.
notes: Glosses—
red silk (xiāo): thin red silk gauze;
wind about (jiǎo rào): to encircle; to twine, to entangle;
flying white: snowflakes scattering on the wind.

yinian/2018-07-13.title: Po Zi Ling · Leaving Blank
stanzas: I have a brush of wind and dust, and I swear to break through — the outline held inside. Idly I discount and trade away the questions of the future; it takes no more than a lock laid on the soul.

People say, who in a former life was without fault — and so with my own hands I hand the heavy burden down and set it aside. From here on I will alter and add: three cries called aloud, one return to settle the debt of karma.

yinian/2018-10-20.title: Lian Qing Shen · Set Free — on the finale of Ruyi's Royal Love in the Palace
stanzas: Always hoping the news will bring a next time with it, never leaving, never forsaking. Orchid cause and catkin fruit teach two people to cherish each other, borrowing the look of helplessness.
Love can hardly last until both heads are white; regret burns its tears to ash. The moonlit night is cold, the solitary heart is scalding, and the green plum hangs low.
notes: Glosses—
orchid cause and catkin fruit: a figure for a marriage beautiful at its beginning and ending in separation;
borrowing: to borrow, to make use of.

yinian/2018-10-20-2.title: Qingse Ru Qingshan · The Days Ahead Are Long
stanzas: Cloud and water do not touch; I lay down the karma of the life before. Sitting in contemplation through ten thousand autumns, the breath transformed blows the blossoms down.
The world of dust has nothing to do with me; the fire at the heart dies back. Now and then the sun's brightness comes out — from the high mountain, one shout.
notes: Glosses—
Qingse Ru Qingshan: the name of a ci tune, also called 'Sheng Zha Zi';
yīng: blossom, flower;

yinian/2018-11-03.title: Lou Shang Qu · Night Coming On
stanzas: Outside the tower a moored boat runs with the waves after the moon; inside the tower someone braces against the battering of the double doors. In a panic, fearing the west wind, guarding the long night; inside the cage of dust a madness breeds.

Often I watch the two shadows flanking the lamp-wick, and with bare hands snap the sword to put down the savage dream. The tall wutong sways, its snow-fragrance soft; the sky turns white, and I am awake alone for countless ages.
notes: Glosses—
put down: to suppress, to hold down;
snow-fragrance: the white flowers of the wutong tree;
countless ages (wàn sī nián): short for yìwàn sī nián, an immense span of years.

stanzas: How good to be at leisure — pleasure comes, and the sun stays long. Tending the little scene of the basin-pond, shuttling busily about the courtyard.

yinian/2018-11-17.title: Qiu Ji · Unwilling to Send Word; a Later Promise Missed
stanzas: The mountains' color is a misty blur; a cold eye takes in wind and haze, and the hanging sleeves snap and crack. Just look at the river's flow, parting Jing from Wei so clearly — but does it know it decays year upon year? After all these years have gone by, reckoning it up, the shooting of tigers must lie far back and long ago. Which of them is ever enough! Following what is right — come from far away, with many lifetimes still to bear and repay.

The gray cliff darkens, everything that meets the eye is murky, grass and trees go rustling, and somewhere a xiao pipe plays on and on. I sigh at the cloud-heights, think of the birds in flight; the blue void comes down to earth and turns its head the wrong way. Do not ask why a person has grown thinner. Do not speak of having no choice, do not covet the jostling human world — I was cold and thin-hearted from the start, half a life marked down.

yinian/2019-03-23.title: Fa Qu Xian Xian Yin · Seen in Vain
stanzas: Not troubling the heart, not hearing, not seeing, pale fingers touches the string and it shivers. Half a lifetime adrift; among the pillows the incense is ash; a flying dove slips into the hidden confinement. Sigh, sigh, sigh — once you have left people behind, who knows the rhyme inside the tune?

A hundred turns and pauses; the tangled strings sorted out, the notes and measures set in order; the heart's business cleared, I lift my eyes and the stream in the ravine sounds close. Eyes shut, I skim past wind and dust, break through the pass of feeling; the orchid pendant swings and shakes. Tears have their warmth and their chill; vexed at the red note-paper, I bear and keep bearing the business of dreams. Again I walk where the tower stands empty, and facing the moon the immortal butterfly beckons me on.
notes: Glosses—
left people behind: to go away from other people;
bear and keep bearing: unable to bear; to endure, to hold oneself in check.

yinian/2019-06-11.title: Qing Yu An · New Life
stanzas: On the green peak, one cup poured warm and then cool. How many times have I plucked at the floss of the yellow flowers. Who governs disaster and blessing and looks after all under heaven — clear frost without regret, feelings hoarded in the pillow, the white moon filling the valley of the spirit.

The orchid oil burns out and leaves the lines of a poem behind; pine-leaf wine, and the fragrant carriage casts off the soft jade. I cannot see which way the wind sets, to follow the right road. Grinding and breaking come round again; a sidelong glance, a crested ibis; the water rises and the wind-gourd floats away.
notes: Glosses—
plucked (miè): to pick at or rub with the fingers;
clear frost: used as a figure for hair gone white;
the pillow: a pillow hollowed out so that things can be hidden inside; hence, to treasure something up;
orchid oil: in antiquity, an oil rendered from the seeds of the marsh orchid; it could be burned in lamps;
pine-leaf: standing here for pine-leaf wine;
wind-gourd: a water dipper; in antiquity often used to stand for the life of a recluse.

yinian/2019-06-15.title: Yi Dian Chun · A Preference
stanzas: Restless with nothing to lean on, I chew the hair-tip of the brush; crabapple blossom mixed in with water-caltrop threads. The lovely colors in the lake have no end at all, and out of the space between the brows the knotted mood loosens and opens.

restless with nothing to lean on: the vexation of a mood that has nothing to rest upon;

stanzas: Enough of this sound upon sound — I smash the konghou. Try to think back: yesterday morning, one dou of rice? Steps turn toward the screen-hills and do not come back; the horse's head lifts toward nothing, and the foolish child waits.

yinian/2019-08-03.title: Kan Hua Hui · A Dream Inside the Dream
stanzas: Under the tree the white ants gather up the light of the years; the flower's tears are flustered. This body ought to have been a wanderer at ease, and yet it stops its words, fallen away into a thousand frosts. The cloud-heights go off with the migrant birds; half a cup, and then waste and ruin.

Brows and eyes can still carry a dimpled smile spreading wide; a painting in bright colors, treasured away. The dream runs after the hollow world and the dusty heart breaks off; for two or three coins, I see straight through the innermost heart. I entrust it all to this morning's warmed wine and the clean fragrance of green plums.
notes: Glosses—
white ants (pífú): another name for the termite;
a thousand frosts: a thousand years; a way of describing a long stretch of time;

yinian/2019-09-18.title: Rui Zhegu · Twin Jade
stanzas: Blocking the road, the storyteller smiles his fawning smile at the Buddha; sea and sky in chaos temper an asura. Ten thousand folded ravines of swords race with the lightning; spring-water and fire in the blind dark, and the white goose is quick.

The great dream of a thousand years is fit to bear the weight; the fragrance ruined across the ground is left to come to nothing. Old memories of former births — push the window open, clear; a broken mirror is hard to make whole, and there is so much that cannot be helped.

yinian/2019-11-16.title: Shishi Ling · Seeking Delight
stanzas: By twos and threes, the snow-slush soaks and spreads across the wide waste. Indulgent, the lamp burns low and sleep is safe from care; whether going or staying, the spring cold has only just come down. Half awake, it weaves itself into a spirit-country that flows on; our eyes meet, and the heart scalds.

The incense ash piles and curls, the threads of wind make their sound, the fluttering slips over a slender palm. The crystal curtain stirs and stirs feeling up; in the mildness and warmth the bright moonlit evening turns to a daze. Year after year I know you are here beside me, and so the constant longing is settled at last.
notes: Glosses—
soaks (yīn): water spreading out and seeping through;
fluttering (zhǎn fú): to flutter and drift; to brush and stir;
bright moonlit evening (lǎng xī): a clear night with a bright moon.

yinian/2020-02-07.title: Anyang Hao · People at Peace — Reflections on the Novel Coronavirus
stanzas: Anyang is good; in a year of ordinary plenty, I cherish the human world. Only when the eye passes over the emptied city, every trace of people gone, do we understand that it was the noise and clamor that raised our homeland. I long for the old rivers and hills.

On the night of the round moon, tea stains dye the golden silkworm. Merit and fault are nothing but the chasing down of right and wrong; the bitter cold is hard to forget, and one dreads sitting idle. On the front line no one has slept.
notes: Glosses—
ordinary good year: 1. a year of ordinary good harvest;
golden silkworm: 1. a silkworm cast in gold; a kind of object buried with emperors in antiquity.

yinian/2020-02-08.title: Qing Bei Le · Heaven and Earth Without Limit
stanzas: Heaven's decree is nonsense; I tear up the register of immortals and throw myself into the eight hundred ways of the world. To be happy is good enough, Buddha or Dao, it makes no difference — I mean to write of unfettered things. Blade raised, astride the horse, killing without pardon; the blood spatters and the flying sand washes it away. In black robes I take shape, hidden in the color of night, putting down the traitors of the imperial city.

Carefully I give out the mineral medicine; the wooden fish is struck until it splits; forgetting home, kin, and self, I pass beyond rebirth. Cupping the wine, I set the shooting stars swaying, read the whole universe in silence, and rise again carrying the splendor of the age. The six realms are level and calm; I tip the cup and drink my fill, and sitting on the bare ground I take a new meaning apart. Joy brings the tears out; as long as the body is here, the meditating heart does not die.
notes: Glosses—
the three forgettings: forgetting home, forgetting kin, forgetting self.

yinian/2020-03-20.title: Zizi Shuang · Easing the Hardship
stanzas: Lamp lit for reading at night, long and long again; album leaves heaped up, basket and basket again. Yellow-ripe aloeswood that sinks in water, fragrant and fragrant again; the soul of the ink lends its color, line and line again.
notes: Glosses—

yinian/2020-03-22.title: Su Zhong Qing · A Joyful Meeting
stanzas: Fine snow, a magpie crying, forms and shadows leaping, the two of us in delight. The sash loosens, flies across, the dimples sweet. Warm in the arms, tightly entwined, the heart at ease. The umbrella shelters a feeling soft as cotton, setting off a tender face.

stanzas: Looking up at the sky, hopeless; camels and horses go down, the fierce sun scorching. Plucking the huqin—not yet old—the vulture wails. Crimson sand rolls over, tears on the fragrant lapel, crying out the sounds of home.

yinian/2020-05-07.title: Qing Ping Le · An Age of Peace and Plenty
stanzas: One old man, one old woman, seated, sipping fish maw. Stir-fried rabbit, its flavor layered with honeyed dates, a long telling of the noisy spring when they first met.

Twice-brewed wine tossed with jade-green florets and sheep's testicles, amber walnuts in a thickened sauce. Sesame flatbread folded around mutton—in this dynasty four eyes meet, the peach tree in full bloom.
notes: Glosses—

Jade-green: here it stands for broccoli;
Twice-brewed [dou]: wine brewed over a second time;

yinian/2020-05-11.title: Lin Jiang Xian · Quick with Spirit
stanzas: At the water's edge, on the windy dike, casting a sidelong glance—a willow whistle drives off the dust and smoke. Slender green shadows outdo the true immortals. Lightly drifting catkins, from the highest heaven.

On the paper the ink runs thick, the sweet-herb scent draws near; damp clouds are slow to move, the billows swirl back. Ice flesh and jade bone contend with the gauze gown. Whose house is so fortunate—color laid along the curved moon of the brows.
notes: Glosses—
Sweet-herb scent [hengwu]: the fragrance of aromatic grasses;
Slow to move [shehuan]: tardy; unhurried;
Swirling billows: waves turning and circling back.

yinian/2020-05-18.title: Bing Di Fu Rong · Half a Life Too Late
stanzas: Dawn moon, no sleep; the dream-rain beats the leaves into disorder; the silver dragon-spout is nearly run dry. White paper stains blue-green; gathering the soul, we come closer still. Knowing well the good and ill that come with the seasons—all things are impermanent, and cannot be resented. Muffled thunder, peal upon peal; thinking of the past—when the swallows left, did they ever once pause?

My love takes on the color of mist; I go after them, the traces are gone; the wheel of rebirth lies across the road. Rinsing ink, steeping the lotus threads, the cold of night is the crueler. Who will make the vow whole again? Half a lifetime estranged, we could hardly know each other now. Don't speak of it, don't ask—as things stand today, there is only more distance between us.
notes: Glosses—
Dream-rain: a fine, blurring drizzle;
Keeping to the season: according with the seasons of heaven;
Silver dragon [yinqiu]: the silver dragon-headed spout at the base of a clepsydra. The clepsydra was an ancient timekeeping device.

yinian/2020-06-21.title: Hou Ting Hua · Passing By
stanzas: Sinking deep into sleep, dream within dream, never gathering up what it all came to. In the back court's deep chambers, plucking a red apricot bloom; the ancient water copies out a shadow.
In the dream, barely through barrier after barrier—a full hundred years and more. Not the heart but the seven-inch spot bears the wordless weight; the indignation quiets a little.
notes: Glosses—
Pluck [xie]: to pick off;
Not [fei]: an adverb, meaning 'not'.

yinian/2020-09-24.title: Yi Qi Ling · Born into This Age
stanzas: Ci. Bearing up, a whole life. Clear sun shining, the ferryboat at rest. Now drinking fruit wine, now singing along with the deer's call. Long pieces talk over the unofficial histories, short lines set down the mood of the heart. Who will join me in inviting the wind and moon—I sigh that this mortal dust so easily comes to nothing. At the sky's edge I do not know where to go; better to look at a thousand autumns of scenery, its sameness and its difference.
notes: Glosses—
Sing along [he]: to join in the singing in harmony;
Sameness and difference: the points in which things differ and in which they agree.

yinian/2020-10-05.title: Ru Sai · This Body a Guest
stanzas: Into the grey mountains, hoping for nothing else—a cold moon hangs. Snow-dust settles close on the shoulder, the horse let loose flashes past the great pass. Longing pulls at me, ten thousand ages stern.

The pipa held in my arms gives the years back; war drums beat—the fire of armies in an instant. The long serpent hisses and roars, stewing the nether springs. Before the hurrying brush, another story is added.
notes: Glosses—
Snow-dust: the fine grains of snow the wind carries with it;
Flash [che]: to streak past at great speed;

yinian/2021-03-21.title: Liu Yao Ling · Two Realms
stanzas: Standing astride two realms, the divine tree grants an early spring. A civet rustles and darts away, making straight for the cherry-blossom butterflies to vex them. A sidelong glance: the wind soft, the snow spreading; sitting in forgetfulness, the clear light grows deep. The dusty world runs to make its report—and in the end, a mind full of the rivers and lakes is all wasted effort.

Longing desperately for the blue luan to fly in, to retire from office and go back to the temple of heaven. Having seen enough of the four seasons' impermanence, at ease, letting the heart shine as it will. I hold the cup and sip the white tea's slender leaves, cutting off the brazier's curling smoke. Ah, to cultivate the Way—asking for no calculation—let me be drunk on the fine hour and the good within it.
notes: Glosses—
Rustling [xī sū]: a faint, fine rustling sound;
Civet: the li. Like a cat but not a cat; older than the cat family;
Ah [yefu]: a modal particle, marking exclamation.

yinian/2021-05-07.title: Jiang Yue Huang Chong Shan · Crape Myrtle
stanzas: Wind and moon have nothing to do with refined amusement; no need for the floating clouds of fame and gain. Far hills, a thin haze holding up the white wheel. The flowers' scent comes early; bright beauty lets the spirit slacken.

The waterfall's clear note breaks off and resumes; before the rock I cup my hands and drink the sweet and pure. Body light, I rise and ride to the wood of happiness. Gathering the blue and purple—once gone far, it is no longer now.
notes: Glosses—
Hold up [ye]: by extension, to support, to prop;
No need [buxiao]: not required, not necessary;

yinian/2021-05-23.title: Yi Hu Zhu · Too Much
stanzas: Settled into an ordinary fate, I wake to find the sea of desire hanging, a hollow void. Impermanent, beginningless, the nature of unknowing. Brahma-mantras in golden light scatter a dream of mermaid pearls.

Old thoughts, drifting affinities, an inch of heart is all that is left; as chance directs, the asura hosts pass into extinction. Karmic fire spreads to the borderless edge and melts the dusty realm. I petition for the god's might, to capture the other side of yin and yang.

stanzas: I have a brush of wind and dust, one lone rider unequalled under heaven. The blue current swallows the desert sea; the sun rising from its bath in the water meets the mountains' spirit.

yinian/2021-11-17.title: Tan Po Huan Xi Sha · Going and Staying
stanzas: Flowers and willows in lush profusion crowd the feather robe; who is meant to guess these delicate thoughts? Before long, on a small raft, I shall roam the blue heavens and reach the numinous pool.
Ask the traveler, all easy and unhurried, and only one answers; the carved mural raises doubt. One step into the rivers and lakes and cause and effect begin; you are bound to be entranced.

Riding a raft [chengfu]: to travel on a small raft of bamboo or wood;

yinian/2022-01-31.title: Jin Cuo Dao · Looking Ahead
stanzas: The debts of the human world drown in dust and sand; where the currents join in the void and the ocean there is nothing else. Travelers at the sky's edge scatter at the sky's edge; affinities go, affinities come, and gather into clear sight.

The blade goes into the sheath, the dream puts out flowers; the roving dragon, keen and fierce, shakes out the cinnabar clouds. The last cold is not yet over, but the heart runs hot; it nurses the spring light and brings the sun's glory forth.
notes: Glosses—
Void and ocean: a Buddhist term, emptiness and the great sea;
The last cold: the chill that lingers after Great Cold, before the warmth returns.

yinian/2022-05-26.title: Zhe Gu Tian · The Primal Beginning
stanzas: I am one unfettered wanderer under heaven; at leisure I step out of the world and ferry across the red dust. I live by grass and trees, rich in wind and water; the ten thousand things all have spirit, and the morning dew is kin.

The mirror of rebirth overturns the common order. Rustling bamboo leaves tell out their low chant; I have never looked back at the shoreless sea—the earth is wide, the mountains high, and I take them for my neighbors.
notes: Glosses—

yinian/2022-11-13.title: Liang Zhou Ling · So It Is Said
stanzas: A path through a thousand mountains, desolate; grieving at heart for the people's long-gathered weakness. Year after year, age after age, the road is the same, and yet once, hair bound up, I chased the fires of war.
Rising, astride the horse, upright as a lance; half a lifetime a stranger away from home. Taking my charge from heaven and earth, I lift my head and see the bamboo waves raging.

yinian/2023-02-12.title: Hua Qian Yin · Planting a Thought
stanzas: Flowers scatter across the courtyard; I raise my cup; the moon shines alone, the long watches thicken the mood. Swaying through the years of youth, drunken eyes pass over the ruined parts of the city.

Ten thousand fathoms of red dust, its affairs hard to refuse; beside a soft fragrance, a clear wind comes to talk. Don't bring up the old memories again; the satin ribbon unrolls, the fire of the years dances.

yinian/2024-05-16.title: Geng Lou Zi · Holding the Game
stanzas: In the evening wood, a desolate moon rippling, every sound of man and horse comes slow. The wind is too still, catching on threads of dust, breathing in and out, luring the dream into its weaving.
The fireflies come back; I turn at the door to look—who else trims the lamp and tries the sword? The stream surges, the pebbles strike; let the lamplight go out as it will.

stanzas: Drifting along as things come, what I have seen and heard is plentiful, and I worry that the days are wasted away. Ah well, two or three matters and no more; looking back, the moments of delight have become yesterday.

stanzas: All at once it turns warm, orioles at play; the green grass chases the butterflies, the mood let loose. Adorning the hours, embroidering a bright dream; a hidden fragrance tugs at the lapel and stirs it.
A thin gown falls into the green shadows; a pale finger lightly lifts the heavy dew. Wanting to come near and still holding back—so many springs of waking—and the human world is of no use.

yinian/2026-06-27.title: Yu Lou Chun · Clamor and Stillness
stanzas: A realm of snow without dust, heaven itself made into a world; a mustard seed holds the mountain and contains the bursting waterfall. On the spirit terrace a thought arises and takes in three thousand worlds; ten thousand ravines, the clear mountain haze floating over a far sea.

Having walked all the passes and rivers, I know the nature of things; half a mouthful of perch broth from the chopsticks hurries the drinking game. The heart all clear and still, idle as the clouds; I lie across the splendid feast and hear a distant chime.
notes: Glosses—
Far [jiong]: remote, distant;
Chopstick [zhu]: chopsticks;
Chime [qing]: an ancient instrument, used mostly in Buddhist temples.

yinian/2026-07-01.title: Qiu Ye Yue · Almost Light, Not Yet Light
stanzas: Cool thoughts fill my sleeves; I close the unfinished book; smoke enters the bed-curtain; the lamp-flower crumbles lightly. I have counted every paulownia leaf at the window, facing an empty quilt. Still weary, the brazier nearly ash, the water-clock still sounding. What is to be done—only that the night is deep and sleep is hard.

The silk curtain like water; the third watch passes; the cup half overturned; this long yearning, what will console it? If the dream comes back, do not ask; there are tears left on the pillow. Words cannot get to the heart of it—this feeling of many years—the scented pouch still hanging there. Turning the thought over, I wait right up to the streak of dawn when the fragrance fades.
notes: Glosses—
Sleeve [mei]: the sleeve of a robe;
Quilt [qin]: a bed quilt;
Silk curtain [luowei]: a bed-curtain woven of silk.
